Aiya, let me think through this year. I have 22.1 mu in total — about 10 mu I keep in cotton on the western plot (the soil there is sandier, cotton does better), about 10 mu where I do wheat then maize back-to-back, and a small 2 mu corner where I put stevia because the buyer from the company comes through the village every year and the price is okay.

My second son and my daughter-in-law work in the city most of the year, they send some money home but they're not here for the planting and harvest. So it's mostly me, my husband, and my eldest son's wife who handle the field work. The grandchildren are in school. For cotton picking I'll have to pay some women from the village to help, that's always the biggest labor cost.

This year I'm doing more or less what I did last year. Last year wheat was alright — got about 420 kg/mu, not bad. Maize was a bit weak because we had that dry spell in August, only 430 kg/mu. Cotton was okay. The stevia company paid us 5 yuan/kg for dried leaves which was decent.

**Wheat** — already planted last October, the seedlings came up fine and survived the winter. Now in spring I need to do my topdress. I put down about 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting (that's the 15-15-15 stuff). Now at jointing I'll spread one bag of urea — that's 50 kg — across about 4 mu, so roughly 12 kg of urea per mu. Some of my neighbors put more but I think that's enough. I'll irrigate 3 times — once now (spring water), once at heading, once when the grain is filling. Each watering costs about 30 yuan/mu for the well electricity. If aphids come at heading, I'll spray, otherwise no.

**Maize** — right after wheat harvest in June, very tight, maybe 5 days. My eldest son's wife and I plant by hand because hiring the planter machine is expensive and our plot is small. Hybrid seed from the agro-shop, the same Zhengdan variety the village uses. I put down compound fertilizer at planting, then topdress urea when the maize is knee-high. If August is dry like last year I'll irrigate once or twice, but it costs money so I wait to see if it rains.

**Cotton** — plant in late April when soil warms up. Cotton is hard work but the price has been okay. I use about 12 kg N per mu — bollworm is always the worry so I budget for spraying 4-5 times in summer. Picking is the headache, I'll need to hire 4-5 women for about 10 days total across the picking season.

**Stevia** — small plot, transplant the seedlings in late April. The company supplies the seedlings. Need more water and care than the grain crops, but per mu the income is better. Cut multiple times.

I keep some cash back for emergencies — if a sprayer breaks or someone gets sick, I can't be empty-handed.
